provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
The input is a lattice of cells at odd coordinates; slicing g[1::2,1::2] gives the compact R x C colour grid. This works in every D4 frame because the input dimensions are odd and the lattice is symmetric. The output is always 26x26 filled with background palette[0]. It has a 2-cell border and 2-cell gaps. Block sizes are (22-2(n-1))/n for n=1..4, which always divides exactly, so the layout is mirror-symmetric and reflections need no special handling. Each non-background cell is painted as a block.

In the generator, same-colour neighbours along the original row axis always have their gap filled, and those cells are marked 'taken'. Same-colour neighbours along the column axis are joined only when neither cell is taken, i.e. both are single-cell runs.

A clockwise rotation by an odd count maps original rows onto visible columns. So the factory picks the always-merge axis from d4 parity: horizontal for even d4%4, vertical for odd. The selective join runs along the other axis. Row reversal (d4>=4) does not change which axis is which. Both merge tests are symmetric, so direction does not matter. Background-coloured cells are treated as empty and never painted. 2x2 same-colour squares are excluded by the generator, so this taken-based rule matches the archived solver's 'identical run span' rule.
draft_notes.limitations: Assumes the constructor's domain: compact grid 1..4 per side, odd-coordinate lattice, a fixed 26x26 output, and background = palette[0]. Demonstrations are not consulted because all roles are fixed by d4 and palette. No contradictions between the fixtures and the uniform rule were found. Not tested by me.
